segments.en: One who studies the books of our great master, the man of G-d, Rabbi Moshe Chaim Luzzatto z"tzal, and other books that engage with Chochmas HaEmes — finds before him, at the beginning of his study, many concepts that are new to him, each with many particulars. The difficulties that stand before him are not only in absorbing and understanding the new concepts in all their many particulars — but the main difficulty is to encompass the things and create from them a general picture and a complete structure.

segments.en: For it is only from seeing the overall structure — which is composed of the system of concepts of Chochmas HaEmes — that one can understand what this wisdom as a whole comes to teach us. (Certainly there are many teachings here, each deeper than the other.) Moreover — even each concept by itself can be properly understood only through grasping the overall picture. For only through discerning the place of each concept within this structure, and understanding its relations and connections with the other concepts — the other parts of the structure — can one arrive at the correct understanding of the concept.

This is one of the main difficulties in this study.

segments.en: Indeed, only with effort and patience can one arrive, with Heavenly help, at this clear understanding — for this one teaches about that one, and one piece of knowledge completes another. And from within the world of chaos and confusion of knowledge not yet fully clear and not yet properly arranged — the World of Tikkun is built and placed, little by little, before the eyes of the student: in it each concept finds its fitting place, and through this — its clear explanation.

segments.en: To what may this be compared? To a person who has never seen a clock and is unfamiliar with how it works. When shown the parts of a disassembled clock and told the nature of each part — the cogs, the screws, the hands, etc. — and when one tries to explain how all its parts work together, he still cannot grasp the nature and manner of working of the clock — as long as he has not seen a complete clock in operation. And he cannot correctly understand the nature and function of each part in this clock.

segments.en: It has happened that Torah scholars began to engage with Chochmas HaEmes — but because of this difficulty discontinued their study, since they had not yet received the overall picture from their engagement with the particulars of the wisdom. A burden of knowledge that is unordered and unclear — became heavy for them, and they had not the patience to persist in this study until they would see over time the fruit of their labour — a comprehensive, ordered structure in which each piece of knowledge would find its proper place.

segments.en: The overall picture of Chochmas HaEmes is called "the Sacred Tree." Just as a tree has roots and a trunk from which the branches emerge and upon which grow the leaves and the fruit — so too Chochmas HaEmes is arranged as a tree in all its parts. In order to know the nature, place, and function of the branches, leaves, and fruit — which are the particulars of the knowledge — one must first sketch the overall picture of the roots and trunk of this tree, which is the overall structure of Chochmas HaEmes. Rabbenu z"tzal sketched this tree for us in the ten chapters of "Klalus HaIlan HaKadosh" and expanded its explanation in the book "Pischay Chochmah VaDaas" — which is "the few that holds the many." But at the beginning we need a more general sketch of this tree — for the beginner: the particulars that Rabbenu included in this tree, even though they are foundational, conceal from his eyes the stature of the main trunk, and he still cannot encompass the overall structure of the tree of Chochmas HaEmes.

segments.en: A further difficulty for one who wishes to study Rabbenu's works engaging with Chochmas HaEmes: already at the beginning of his study he expects illuminating explanations of the content and meaning of Chochmas HaEmes — like one who studies Gemara and wants to enjoy and delight in the explanations of the great commentators before he has grasped the flow of the sugya and the simple meaning of the words. But the difficulty is even greater in Chochmas HaEmes — for it was transmitted to us in a system of concepts entirely new to us, and at the beginning of our study we have no foothold in it. This system was transmitted to us in the language of mashal;2 and Rabbenu calls it "the vision"3 — for so the prophets saw and envisioned it. The explanations of the nimshal — "the solution" in Rabbenu's terminology — can be well understood only when one knows the mashal thoroughly — its structure and the multiplicity of its concepts and particulars.

segments.en: We have seen prominent Torah scholars who began to study the book Klah Pischay Chochmah — which deals with the explanations of the nimshal, and contains also descriptions of the mashal — who saw at first a great light in the wondrous explanations of the nimshal. But in the course of their learning they came to realise that things were still not clear to them — for they did not know the overall structure of the mashal. Therefore they could not arrange and connect each piece of knowledge and explanation of the nimshal to that part of the mashal to which it relates. And they grew weary in this study. Indeed, of Chochmas HaEmes it is said with even greater force: "First review, and then reason deeply" [based on Avodah Zarah 19a] — as Rabbenu himself emphasises at the end of his essay "Derech Eitz HaChaim." First one must review the mashal deeply — and then one merits, with G-d's help, to understand the nimshal.

segments.en: In order to ease the "first review" of the mashal — we have endeavoured with Heavenly help to give together with the general survey of the structure of the mashal — also brief explanations of the nimshal, to the extent that they pertain to this survey, as they emerge from Rabbenu's Torah. Certainly, as stated, the basis for correct understanding of Chochmas HaEmes is the "first review" of the mashal — even if at the beginning the student does not yet understand the nimshal. According to the labour is the reward — in the course of study Hashem will open for him the gates of understanding, and he will understand Rabbenu's Torah and his illuminating explanations of the mashal, and the mashal and nimshal will become clearer to him together — as they come to teach one another.

segments.en: His light, blessed be He,4 is infinite — without boundary or measure. It fills all, and relative to it no other existence is possible — "there is nothing other than it." At the very beginning of the creation of the world, Hashem contracted for our sake a part of His light, giving it boundary and measure — in order to allow existence to Creation and to the created beings, and so that we, the limited created beings, could attain something of His radiance. Tzimtzum (contraction) is from the language of covering — as the Sages of blessed memory used it: "and she covered her face" [Bereishis Rabbah end of ch. 45]5 — that is, Hashem covers Himself toward us, and reveals to us only limited revelations; but He Himself — no Tzimtzum or boundary applies to Him. The measure and degree of the Tzimtzum is such as to allow the possibility of the formation of darkness, matter, body, and evil — which create the possibility of serving Hashem through struggle and through choice between good and evil.

segments.en: The Sefiros are the revelation of His attributes, blessed be He — His ways and governances — to which the Creator gave measure, quantity, and number through the Tzimtzum. Therefore they are called Sefiros. Their name is also explained from the meaning of sapir — the sapphire stone that has no colour of its own, yet the rays of light sparkle within it in a variety of rainbow colours. So too the Sefiros — to us they are perceived as multi-coloured, in number and in measure — while His light, blessed be He, in and of itself admits of no division into colours, number, or limitation.

segments.en: His governances, blessed be He, divide into ten roots — ten Sefiros. They themselves divide into three groups of three Sefiros: Keser-Chochmah-Binah; Chesed-Din-Rachamim (also: Gedulah-Gevurah-Tiferes); Netzach-Hod-Yesod. And at the end of all of them: the tenth Sefirah — Malchus. In each group there are two Sefiros standing at the two extremities — right and left — and the third is intermediate between them. In each group the right Sefirah is in the aspect of Chesed — the influencer and giver. The left Sefirah is in the aspect of Din — the one that constricts; and relative to the right it has an aspect of receiver, limited according to its capacity for receiving. Between the two — the third Sefirah, intermediate between the two extremities. The three groups form a structure of three tiers of the attributes of His governance, with each tier having two Sefiros at the two extremities and a third intermediate Sefirah.

segments.en: The upper tier is arranged in the form of an inverted segol — Keser at the top with Chochmah and Binah beneath it. Keser stands at the head of the structure — for it encompasses the "purpose" of the entire structure — contained in the beginning of the thought, as the final purpose arises in His will in the aspect of "the end of the deed was first in thought." From it flow the remaining Sefiros, leading to the actualisation of the purpose of His governance. Since Keser encompasses the entire structure in the aspect of will and root — therefore its place is at the head of all the Sefiros, in the central column. Chochmah is the thought in broad strokes of how to carry out the will. Binah details and formulates these principles into detailed paths of execution.

segments.en: Sometimes Da'as is counted in place of Keser. According to this, the upper tier is arranged in the form of a segol: Chochmah — Da'as — Binah. Da'as appears in the middle, below Chochmah and Binah, for it flows from them. Da'as is the attribute of application of Chochmah and Binah — it transfers the conclusions of Chochmah and Binah to the remaining Sefiros, penetrating into them until it becomes their inner dimension.6 From the perspective of the relation of the ten Sefiros to the source — to the "world" or "Partzuf" above them — Keser is counted (as it is above the head of the King); while from the perspective of the influence of the head (= Chochmah and Binah) upon the Sefiros below them — Da'as is counted.

segments.en: The seven lower Sefiros constitute the structure of governance in actuality — the body of governance. They are mentioned in Scripture [Divray HaYamim I, 29:10]: "Yours, Hashem, is the greatness (=Chesed) and the might (=Din) and the splendour (=Rachamim) and the eternity and the majesty — for all that is in heaven and in earth (=Yesod) — Yours, Hashem, is the kingdom (=Malchus)." The principal attributes — their place is in the centre of the structure, in the second tier. They are arranged in a segol: Chesed and Din at the two sides, and below them in the middle: Rachamim (= Chesed-Din-Rachamim, or Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferes). These three Sefiros constitute the principal governance. Chesed is abundant and broad influence. Din constricts and limits the influence according to the deeds and merits of the receiver — and is also called Gevurah in the aspect of subduing and constricting ("Who is mighty? One who subdues his inclination"). Rachamim is the balanced equilibrium between these two extremities — and is also called Tiferes, for this is the governance in the splendour of its completeness, bringing Chesed and Din together in coordination and harmony. This attribute is also called Emes — Truth — for this is governance in the correct and precise balance, without veering right or left.

בדרכים שונים 1047אינ ם אל א תיקון כל מה הוא שורש לאדם, 1048 למען יושפע מכולו , 049שפע ברכה על הנ שמה ההיא; כ א שי ל ^ 9א זה ה תיקון — יו שפע ה שפע לנצח בו ,כי עד ה ת הי ה תקבל הנ שמה לבדה , ,070ואחר כך גם הגוף ,עד אין תכלי ת., 07, ותדע שבעבור ענין זה של הגלגול לא יבאו נר״ן ח״י בפעם א חת072י ,אלא כל אחד ואחד יבא בפני עצמו בזמנו .ויש מי שיוכל לקבל כל הנר״ן ח״יג07י ,ומי שלא יוכל ,והפרטים רבים( .ע״כ נמצא בכתבי יד ,וההמשך הוא בנדפס).
segments.en: The lower tier is formed by the Sefiros of the third grouping: Netzach-Hod-Yesod. They transmit and adapt for the created beings the governance of Chesed-Din-Rachamim7 — because as long as human beings have not completed the work of rectifying their deeds, the world cannot stand in the root attribute of Chesed — it cannot endure the abundance of goodness; nor can the world stand under the demands of the root attribute of Din — it cannot endure the abundance of adversity;8 nor has it yet arrived at the perfect equilibrium of the attribute of Tiferes. Therefore, so long as the world is not yet rectified, these Sefiros operate — in which the root Sefiros are blended. Sefirah of Netzach: Chesed with a blend of Din — from it flows the governance of "the righteous who suffers" — Hashem in His Chesed collects his debts in this world in order to grant him merit for the World to Come. Sefirah of Hod: Din with a blend of Chesed — from it flows the governance of "the wicked who prospers" — his merits are not lost through the force of Din but are paid to him in this world.9 Sefirah of Yesod — also called the attribute of "All" ("for all that is in heaven and earth") — it gathers all the actions of the entire wide spectrum of the attributes from end to end, in order to transmit all the abundance and influence to the lower beings who receive — to the tenth Sefirah: Malchus.

פתי״ד יי׳קכ
segments.en: Sefirah of Malchus ("Yours, Hashem, is the kingdom") is positioned below the Sefirah of Yesod, for it receives from it. It receives all the abundance in order to actualise through it, in Creation, the purpose of the governance of the nine Sefiros above it — the revelation of His kingship, blessed be He. And this needs to be done principally by the lower beings — by human beings. Therefore the Sefirah of Malchus is the root of created beings, and it oversees them and governs them according to the degree of their acceptance of His kingship. It is the aspect of the "Shechinah" that dwells within Yisrael — it is the bond between them and the Holy One Blessed be He.10

פחו״ד סי׳ קפא
segments.en: To illustrate the ten Sefiros with a parable: the desire arises in a person to build a house for a certain purpose. In this desire everything of the house is already encompassed in the aspect of "the end of the deed was first in thought" — this is the aspect of Keser. The architect who plans the house with all its floors, wings, and rooms is in the aspect of Chochmah. The engineer who plans each and every detail — the types of materials and their quantities — is in the aspect of Binah. After them come the attributes of execution — in the above parable: the various craftsmen who do the framework, the plastering, the floors, etc. — this is the aspect of the six lower Sefiros: Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferes, Netzach-Hod-Yesod. The one who enters the house to dwell in it and make use of all that is in it, corresponding to the purpose of the structure — this is the aspect of Malchus, which receives the abundance from the nine Sefiros. The connection: Keser to Malchus — head with end — corresponds to the degree to which the execution matches the intention of the planner. The Sefirah of Da'as is like the function of the general contractor who gives instructions to the various craftsmen according to the plans of the architect and engineer, and stands over their proper execution.

segments.en: According to the above, the nine Sefiros of His governance, blessed be He, form three tiers vertically — one upon the other — the upper one being greater in kind and quality than the lower. On the other hand, they also form three groups horizontally — three columns: right, left, and centre. In the right column stand the Sefiros of Chochmah, Chesed, and Netzach — this is the column in the aspect of Chesed. In the left column stand the Sefiros of Binah, Gevurah, and Hod — this is the column in the aspect of Din. And in the central column stand the Sefiros of Keser, Tiferes, Yesod, and Malchus — they are in the aspect of the intermediate column between the extremities.

segments.en: Each Sefirah also subdivides into ten Sefiros (for example: the Keser of Keser, the Binah of Keser, etc.) — and so on. When various systems of ten Sefiros are spoken of (in different worlds and different Partzufim) — the intention is not different, separate Sefiros, but the same ten Sefiros at different levels and in different aspects.

segments.en: The totality of all His governances, blessed be He, is called a world. His governances — reflected and operated on different planes in different modes — are the different worlds. For example: on the plane of the physical world — our world — all His governances operate in the ways of our world, the ways of matter. The Sefirah of Chesed is revealed in physical abundance and blessing, while the Sefirah of Din is revealed in the constriction of physical abundance — to the point of want and deficiency. In the spiritual world the same governances are expressed in a spiritual way — spiritual abundance or constriction of spirituality. But we must not think that there is only one spiritual world — as it might seem to us from our limited perspective. Rather there are many different spiritual worlds, one higher than another, more radiant and more pure. The higher a world — the purer and more spiritual the created beings in it. Principally the worlds divide into four: our world — the World of Asiyah (Action) (encompassing the material creatures and their spiritual roots — the appointed ministers over them); above it — the World of Yetzirah (Formation); above it — the World of Briyah (Creation); and above all of them — the World of Atzilus (Emanation) (= A"B"Y"A).11

segments.en: There is a great difference between the World of Atzilus and the worlds of B"Y"A — in that in B"Y"A there are spiritual and physical creatures (spiritual ones in the worlds of Briyah and Yetzirah and the beginning of the World of Asiyah). But in the World of Atzilus there are no creatures at all — in it is the totality of His lights, which reflect His governances. The creatures of the worlds of B"Y"A were created by the Creator as an existence separate from the Creator — as creatures that appear with their own independent being. Therefore they are called "the separated worlds." But the World of Atzilus, as stated, is a world of the modes of His governances — in it all His governances are in the aspect of His thought, revealing to us through His radiations — not yet at the stage of execution — of creatures. Therefore this world is called Atzilus — from the word etzel (beside, at) — still not separated from Him; and also from the word hatzel (emanation) — for from it the worlds of B"Y"A were emanated and created.12 This is a pure spiritual world from whose lights — in their orders and varieties — we learn all His ways, blessed be Him. The prophets envisioned through prophetic vision the brilliantly shining lights whose splendour was reflected in their souls — and they explained them to us in their prophecies — and they are explained in Chochmas HaEmes.13

segments.en: The general principle is: everything that is in one world repeats itself in the world below it — according to the nature of that world — and descends from the world above it. Everything from the World of Atzilus in terms of His ways, blessed be He, has a counterpart in the worlds of Briyah and Yetzirah — spiritual creatures that emerge from and execute His governances; and in the World of Asiyah — physical creatures that are also rooted in His governances (for example: parallel to the attribute of Din and the attribute of Rachamim in the World of Atzilus, there exist in the World of Yetzirah angels of Din and Rachamim, and in the World of Asiyah — physical creatures of Din and Rachamim, creatures that cause harm and creatures that bring abundance and blessing).

ו מ ח״ ל
segments.en: Man is called a microcosm — for he encompasses within himself, in a miniaturised and concentrated form, all that is in the great world. Just as in every world all His governances, blessed be He, are reflected according to the aspect of that world — so too all His governances are reflected in the structure of man's soul,14 and also in the structure of his body (for example: because there exists the oversight of Hashem — "the eyes of Hashem" — man therefore has eyes; because in His governance there are two principal paths — Chesed and Din — which are the aspects of right and left — therefore most of man's limbs are doubled — to the right and to the left).15 This is what Scripture means when it says man was created in His likeness and image — and as is known, this refers to His governances — not to His essence, of which we have no apprehension whatsoever. His likeness and image — these are the structure of the totality of His governances — ten Sefiros branching and dividing into 613 particulars — after the fashion and measure of a human figure with his 613 limbs and sinews. But it is more accurate to say the reverse: that the figure of man with all his limbs and their functions corresponds to the form and image of His governances — for it descends and flows from them — as it is said that man was created in His likeness and image.16

קיצור השתלשלות העולמות ובנין הפרצופים

שמכיל עיקר שרשי חכמת האמת
segments.en: One can perceive what is happening inside a person's soul through the expression of his face — that is, through his partzuf (face) one discerns the nature and character of the person. Therefore the structure of the Sefiros — arranged in the measure of human stature — is called a Partzuf — for it expresses all the inner dimension.

segments.he:
בעשרה פרקים בלשון המשנה

ומצורף לו ציור האילן הקדוש

מאת רבנו הגדול
segments.en: A complete governance is composed of ten Sefiros. But one of the Sefiros can itself be a complete governance according to its aspect and nature — and then that Sefirah subdivides into ten particular Sefiros, and from these is composed a Partzuf with 613 parts, in the measure of a human figure. For example: the Sefirah of Keser — when it encompasses all the Sefiros and governs them as the ultimate will that encompasses and directs all stages of planning and execution — it operates as a Partzuf (Arich Anpin) with its 613 limbs. And so too the Sefirah of Chochmah can operate as the encompasser and includer of all governance from the perspective of planning — from the vantage of Chochmah it oversees Chesed, Din, and the other attributes, planning them according to the reasons and rationale of wisdom. In this aspect of governance, Chochmah constitutes a Partzuf (the Partzuf of Abba) with all the limbs and particulars of the human figure. And so for the other Sefiros, as will be explained below.

תשמ״ט
segments.en: The higher Partzuf clothes itself through its lower part into the Partzuf below it. Through this it influences it and governs it. In the lower part of the Partzuf its lights diminish — therefore only it enters into the Partzuf below — for its lights that diminished there are adapted to the capacity of the lower Partzuf to receive them. Through the clothing, the action of the upper becomes revealed in the lower — just as clothing reveals something of the nature of the person who wears it. On the other hand, the clothed one is concealed and hidden by the garment — so the Partzuf that clothes itself is concealed within the Partzuf that clothes it — for the actions of the upper are not revealed directly, but only through the lower Partzuf — which is governed by the power of the upper Partzuf.

segments.en:
After explaining several basic concepts, we shall give, with G-d's help, a general survey of the picture of the Tree and its branches — skipping over particulars even when they are important in themselves — so as not to burden the eye of the reader in grasping the overall picture. Each particular is explained in its place in Rabbenu's works, in the book Pischay Chochmah VaDaas and in the work Klalus HaIlan, and in Klalei Chochmas HaEmes. For the sake of the flow of the discussion we shall sometimes need to repeat certain things already explained above.

Hashem contracted His light — which is without boundary or measure — and created within the infinite light the void: a limited place where there remained a contracted light within a boundary and measure, according to the need of creating the worlds. Around this limited place, the infinite light remains as it was — upon which the Tzimtzum and the boundary do not apply. The contracted light is called the Reshimu — for it is only like the remains and a small impression of the unlimited light. Into this Reshimu enters a line of light (kav) from the unlimited light that surrounds the limited place — in order to strengthen the light of the Reshimu and complete it.17 Thus, already at the very beginning of Creation, the two extremities of illumination and concealment were established — an illuminating line and a light-contraction: which are the roots of expansion and limitation, influence and contraction of influence, Chesed and Din, right and left, inner dimension and outer dimension, light and vessel, the influencing completor and the receiving deficient one needing completion, male and female, spirit and matter, soul and body, good and evil. All these matters create — through the combination of the two extremities — the possibility of creating the human being composed of body and soul, matter and spirit, giving him the possibility of choice between good and evil — between the dominance of the soul over the body or the reverse, G-d forbid. Naturally, the first stage of the contraction of the light and the illumination of the line — is only the first subtle root of all these matters that descend and flow from this root stage after stage. This is the purpose of the chain-descent and the fall — world after world, contraction after contraction: to prepare the possibility of service through choice for man in our world — the world of concealment and darkness, matter and body.

הקדמה לציור האילן הק׳
segments.en: The line illuminated within the Reshimu — and in combination with the Reshimu (for in all of Creation the actions of these two extremities are combined) — consolidated the first ten Sefiros in the form of circles. As the line entered the place of the Tzimtzum — at the beginning of its entry it formed the first circle within the round place of Tzimtzum: this is the Sefirah of Keser. As it continued to enter — it formed a circle again, creating within the circle of Keser the second circle: the Sefirah of Chochmah. And so it continued to enter, forming circles one within another: the Sefiros of Binah, Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferes, Netzach, Hod, Yesod — and in the centre: the circle of Malchus, the centre of all the circles — the execution of the intention of Creation: the revelation of His kingship, through which we merit the benefit — to enjoy the radiance of the Shechinah, the radiance of the glory of His kingship.

הקדמת לאיוי האילן
segments.en: The formation of circles one within another — one after another — indicates a relation of chain-descent between them. The outer circle that precedes and encompasses the inner circle is a cause to it: from within the Sefirah of Keser — which is the purpose aimed at in His will — flows and comes the Sefirah of Chochmah — the overall planning of the execution of the purpose; from it the Sefirah of Binah — the planning of the particulars; from it the Sefirah of Chesed — the execution of the purpose to influence Chesed upon the created beings; from it the Sefirah of Gevurah and Din — for in order for the Chesed to be complete, man receives the abundance according to his deeds — through Din — and not as an unearned gift. But the world cannot endure by the attribute of Din — therefore the attribute of Rachamim is required — Din blended with Chesed; and so on.

פרק ראשון
segments.en: These ten circles are the ten root Sefiros of the general Providence — which provides some existence to Creation and to nature in all periods and conditions of height and depth — as a constant framework within which man can do his service. Therefore the form of these Sefiros is circles — in which there is no right or left — merit or liability, above or below — ascent or descent. And so the first place of Tzimtzum is round — for the granting of possibility of place and existence through the concealment of His exclusive unlimited light — is equal for all of Creation.18

עד שלא נברא העולם הי ה הוא ושמו אחד .רצה וצמצם

א.
segments.en: The line creates within the Reshimu another order of ten Sefiros in the aspect of uprightness. The ten Sefiros of uprightness are arranged in three straight vertical columns (as explained above in the section "Sefiros"). Right column: Chochmah, Chesed, Netzach. Left column: Binah, Gevurah, Hod. Central column: Keser at the head between Chochmah and Binah; Tiferes between Chesed and Gevurah; Yesod between Netzach and Hod; and below all of them — Malchus. This arrangement is called "the human figure" — for the three uppermost Sefiros are in the aspect of the head: Keser is the skull encompassing the right and left brain — which are Chochmah and Binah. The seven lower Sefiros are in the aspect of the bodily limbs: Chesed and Gevurah — the two arms; Tiferes — the torso; Netzach and Hod — the two legs; Yesod and Malchus — the end of the body. "From my flesh I behold G-d" — from the structure of the body we learn of His governances — as explained above.

ב.

הרא שון שבכולם — אדם קדמון .וממה שעבל בפנים יו צ אי ם ארבע חושים חלק ממנו :ר אי ה ,שמיעה ,ריח ,דבור( .פרק כט) ד׳ או תיו ת הוי״ה ב״ה — ד׳ מלואים :ע״ב ,ס״ג ,מ״ה ,כ ץ —
segments.en: The arrangement of the Sefiros of uprightness is the root of the individual governance and Providence — which governs man according to his deeds. Therefore it has right and left — a side of merit and a side of liability — above and below: ascent and descent. The two systems of Sefiros — circles and uprightness — operate together for the maintenance and advancement of the world. Therefore it is described that the Sefiros of uprightness are embedded within the Sefiros of the circles.19

segments.en: The first structure of the Sefiros of uprightness is Adam Kadmon (A"K) — it is like a fifth world above the worlds of A"B"Y"A. It is called Adam Kadmon — for it is the primordial one relative to the figures of man in the other worlds, and it encompasses all His governances in a more elevated and concealed manner than the World of Atzilus.

segments.en: Adam Kadmon is the World of Reward — and relative to it — the World of Atzilus and the worlds below it: Briyah, Yetzirah, Asiyah — are the worlds of service. The World of Reward preceded in the order of creation the worlds of service — for the service was given for the sake of receiving the reward. And since the purpose of Creation is to benefit — to allow the creatures to enjoy the radiance of the Shechinah in ultimate pleasure — the World of Reward constitutes the root and source of all Creation in the aspect of "the end of the deed was first in thought." We are thus taught that Adam Kadmon encompasses all of Creation in the aspect of root — and all the worlds flow from it. It is the root and trunk of the Tree — and they are branches to it.

segments.en: The Branches of Adam Kadmon

ג.

ד.
segments.en: In A"K we do not yet discern particulars as in the other worlds — and all that is said of it is only by way of analogy from what we understand from the lower orders. As stated, he himself is entirely beyond our apprehension — for the reward: "No eye has seen, O G-d, except You, what He will do for those who await Him" [Yeshayahu 64:3]. We speak only in allusion of the branches that emerge from him — what is revealed from the aspect of his senses: from the eyes, ears, nose, and mouth (the senses of sight, hearing, smell, and speech). Just as man's senses are openings to the outer world — so too the senses of Adam Kadmon are the openings through which the influence passes from his inner dimension to the worlds. (Man, however, absorbs impressions from outside through his senses — whereas A"K projects his abundance through them outward.) There are additionally greater radiations — flowing from the aspect of the skull of A"K: from his thought through his hairs — this is the revelation of the world of eternity, of which we have absolutely no apprehension.

Our Sages of blessed memory stated [Sanhedrin 97a]: "Six thousand years does the world exist and one is destroyed" — the years of service of the created beings are six thousand years. The seventh millennium is the passage from the World of Service to the World of Reward. After them and following them come the Worlds of Reward in the eighth and ninth millennia — from which one ascends to the World of Eternity — from the tenth millennium onward — in the aspect of the lights that emerge from the skull of A"K.

ו.

segments.en: From the ears emerge ten Sefiros, ten radiations — the World of Reward of the ninth millennium. From the nose emerge ten radiations — the World of Reward of the eighth millennium. From the mouth emerge ten radiations — the seventh millennium — of which it is said: "and one is destroyed" — in the aspect of "the ruin of the body is the building of the intellect" (in the words of the Rambam in his introduction to his commentary on the Mishnah) — the soul rules and the body still exists in some form, but ceases to operate. This is as stated the passage from the World of Service to the World of Reward. These lights that flow from his senses descend around him — reaching as far as the midpoint of the stature of A"K. Until here are the stages of the World of Reward.20

ח.
segments.en: From the midpoint of the stature of A"K downward begins the chain-descent of the World of Service. These are the ten Sefiros that emerged from the eyes21 of A"K — in the aspect of the eyes of Hashem that oversee in order to give each one according to his service. These lights that descended from the eyes are discernible only below the midpoint of the stature of A"K — for above him the great lights of ear-nose-mouth shine and dominate. Therefore it is only in the lower part of A"K that the first roots of the paths of service begin to take form. In the lights of the eyes are rooted the Worlds of Service: Atzilus, Briyah, Yetzirah, Asiyah.

segments.en: Atik

segments.he:
— ירדו עם הנ שברים לקיימם .כל היורד — מירידתם של מלכים הוא יורד ,וכל החוזר ועולה — מחזרתם הוא חוזר. ובסופן של דברים מה הוא אומר :והיה אור הלבנה כאור החמה ,וגו׳; ואומר :ביום חבוש ה׳ א ת שבר עמו ומחץ מכתו ירפא — רפואה שאין א חריה מכה; ואומר :ומ שתי א ת עון הארץ ה הי א ביום אחד; ואומר :והי ה ה׳ למלך על כל הארץ ביום ההוא יהי ה ה׳ אחד ושמו אחד( .פרק מ ח

פרק שלישי
segments.en: The principle is: the end of the higher level becomes the beginning and head of the lower level — for example: the Sefirah of Malchus of the higher world becomes Keser for the world below it and governs it. So too the Malchus of A"K becomes the head and Keser for the World of Atzilus. In order to clothe itself in the World of Atzilus and govern it, the Malchus of A"K is built into a Partzuf with all its particulars and parts — and is called "Atika Kadisha" (= A"K) or Atik. Atik is therefore the first Partzuf — (therefore called Atik: the ancient one) — in which we discern the human measure of stature with all its limbs and parts. (A"K is called man only by analogy — for we have no apprehension of its particulars.) Its seven lower Sefiros clothe themselves within the World of Atzilus. But its three upper Sefiros — Keser, Chochmah, Binah — which are the aspect of its head — are above the World of Atzilus, and we do not know their particulars; therefore they are called Reisha d'Lo Isyada — the Head That Is Not Known. In Reisha d'Lo Isyada are rooted the reasons of the World of Service — through them it is established what reward is due for this service and what reward for that; what portion in the general task of rectifying Creation each one receives — and according to this, what means (length of life, wisdom, livelihood, etc.) each one receives for carrying out his particular role. These principles of Providence are hidden from our understanding — and also are not needed for our service. Moreover, knowing them would interfere with our service — for it would diminish our freedom of choice if all were clear to us. Since Atik establishes each person's role — in that light it also establishes to what degree each fulfilled his role — and from this flows what reward is due him. Therefore Atik is what connects the World of Service to the World of Reward — the worlds of A"B"Y"A to A"K. Hence another meaning of atik — connector and transferer — in two directions: establishes according to the reward planned in advance (which is the goal) the fitting service as the means of attaining it; and on the other hand, transfers the results of the service to the corresponding reward due for it.

ב.

ג.
segments.en: Every world is composed of ten general Sefiros according to the aspect and place of that world. From the ten Sefiros are built all the Partzufim of that world. Five are the principal Partzufim — each being a complete governance according to the nature of the Sefirah from which the Partzuf is built, as explained above in the section "Sefirah — Partzuf — The Form of Man."

לאחוריו .פני מ״ה לפניו ,ופני ב״ן לאחוריו .נמצא עתיק כולו פנים. נתקן אריך דו״נ ,הזכר בימינו והנוקבא בשמאלו .תיקונו של א״א
segments.en: The World of Atzilus is composed of the ten general Sefiros which constitute the structure of the totality of His governances, blessed be He. From them are built five Partzufim: from the Sefirah of Keser — the Partzuf of Arich Anpin; from the Sefiros of Chochmah and Binah — the Partzufim of Abba and Imma; from the Sefiros of Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferes-Netzach-Hod-Yesod — the Partzuf of Zair Anpin (explained in the chapter on Zair Anpin below — why from these six Sefiros one Partzuf alone is built); from the Sefirah of Malchus — the Partzuf of Nukva. There are additional Partzufim which are branches of the above Partzufim and secondary to them — explained in their places in Rabbenu's works. We shall explain the five principal Partzufim.

ו.

של א״א .בנינ ם ממ״ה וב״ן ,ו תי קוני ה ם מ אורו תיו של אריך. מג׳ פרקיהם של זרועות לחב״ד שלהם ,ומת״ת ל שאר כל גופם. ומג׳ פרקים רא שונים של חג׳׳ת לע שות מו חותיהם כאחד, מפרקים שניים לחג״ת שלהם ,מפרקים שלי שיים לנה״י שלהם. פרקו הרא שון של ימין מתלבש ברא שו של אבא ,כנגדו בשמאל באימא ,שני לו בחג״ת של זה חה ,שלי שי לו בנה״י, והת״ת נכסה תחתיהן מאליו עד החזה( .פרק 0 או״א — מ״ה וב״ן ב שניהם .נתחברו זה בזה ,נתן אבא ב״ן

ז.
segments.en: The first and central Partzuf in the World of Atzilus is Arich Anpin (= A"A) — it is built from the general Sefirah of Keser of Atzilus (for the Partzuf of Atik belongs to A"K, which is above the World of Atzilus). The Sefirah of Keser encompasses the entire purpose — so too A"A brings Creation to its purpose and perfection. A"A is the central beam that runs from end to end — from the head of Atzilus to its end — spanning the entire measure of the height of Atzilus. As his name says: the long face — a long Partzuf. The other Partzufim are arranged around him, each clothing a part of him. In order to connect Atzilus to the Worlds of Reward, the seven lower Sefiros of Atik clothe themselves within A"A — as explained above. Arich Anpin brings the World of Service to its purpose — to the complete beneficence — when everything comes to its rectification; and he makes use of the other Partzufim that clothe him as means to bring everything to completion. Therefore A"A embraces the entire World of Atzilus. This governance is hidden and inner within the revealed governance of the other Partzufim — which clothe and cover A"A and he is concealed within them. His head is not clothed by the other Partzufim — for in it is the primary part of his governance, elevated above all other governances; from it comes the governance of unity that annuls when necessary the governance of judgment and influences goodness from a treasury of unearned gift even for the wicked — through the activation of the thirteen attributes of mercy.22

ט.
segments.en: Abba and Imma (= Av"A) are the Partzufim built from the general Sefiros of Chochmah and Binah of the World of Atzilus. They clothe the upper part of A"A — from the end of the head (for the head of A"A is not clothed) to his midpoint. They influence from the complete beneficence — which prevails mainly in the upper part of A"A (for in the lower part of every Partzuf his lights diminish) — to the Partzufim below them: Zair Anpin and Nukva (= Zu"N). In the aspect of father and mother they beget and raise Zu"N — who are their children. The first root of Zu"N is in A"A — for the governance of judgment executed by Zu"N has its root in the attribute of complete beneficence — in A"A — which wants to benefit creatures with complete benefit: that they should merit reward through their service and effort, not as an unearned gift accompanied by shame. In actuality the begetters are Av"A. They plan the paths of judgment and give the reasons for judgment — how each particular in it leads to complete beneficence.23 After Av"A have begotten Zu"N, they also guide them with wisdom and understanding — stage by stage — toward perfection. For the sake of the governance and completion of Zair Anpin, the Netzach-Hod-Yesod of Imma (within which the NHY of Abba is clothed) clothe themselves within the Partzuf of Z"A,24 as explained below.

segments.en: Zair Anpin (= Z"A) is the Partzuf of the governance of judgment — for it is built from the general Sefiros of the World of Atzilus: Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferes (= ChG"T) which are the three principal Sefiros of the governance of judgment. Also the Sefiros Netzach-Hod-Yesod (= NHY) of Atzilus participate in his structure — for they adapt the governances of Chesed-Din-Rachamim to the governance in actuality in this world (as explained above in the section "Sefiros"). Since Z"A is composed of six general Sefiros of Atzilus — ChG"T, NHY — he is also called the "six extremities" (= V"K). Each of these Sefiros does not constitute a Partzuf by itself — unlike Keser, Chochmah, and Binah — but all of them together constitute one Partzuf — for each one is only one part or side (one of the six extremities) of the governance of judgment. One of them alone cannot encompass a complete governance — only through the joint operation of these six Sefiros together is the governance of judgment composed.

segments.en: Zair Anpin clothes A"A from his midpoint downward — and through this Z"A reaches the height of the midpoint of the World of Atzilus (therefore called Zair Anpin — small face — a smaller Partzuf). A"A clothes himself within Z"A as a hidden governance operating in every event and in every response of the governance of judgment to the deeds of human beings — to direct them toward rectification and purpose — in a manner hidden from our eyes and understanding. Only in the future, when the redemption comes, will the governance of A"A be revealed to all eyes. This is the governance of unity — the absolute will of the Creator that brings everything — even evil — to rectification.

segments.en: The Partzuf of Z"A — built from the Sefiros of ChG"T, NHY — becomes a Partzuf with ten Sefiros when they subdivide into ten particular Sefiros, as every Partzuf has. But at the beginning only the six lower Sefiros from among his ten particular Sefiros operate in Z"A.25 This is his state of katnus (smallness). The three upper Sefiros — Chochmah-Binah-Da'as (ChB"D)26 — which are his Mochin (intellect), are not yet developed in him and do not yet operate. Through Av"A he arrives at gadlus (maturity) — through their influence his Mochin develop and grow. Just as father and mother raise their child and educate him until he becomes mature and capable of standing independently — so too Z"A perfects his Mochin through the NHY of Av"A clothing themselves within him. Through them Z"A receives his Mochin — so that he can operate with all ten of his Sefiros perfectly, with knowledge and understanding. The Sefirah of Keser — which is the skull encompassing the Mochin — Z"A receives through A"A. In His governances, blessed be He — the state of katnus is a state of concealment of face and exile — when the perfection of His governance is not recognised. While the state of gadlus is a state of revelation of face and redemption — when all recognise the wisdom and greatness of His governances. Also in the cycle of the seasons of the year there are states of katnus and gadlus — states of decrease and increase of spiritual abundance — in weekdays and in Shabbos and Festivals.

ד.
segments.en: The Partzuf of Nukva is built from the general Sefirah of Malchus of the World of Atzilus. She is the root of the receivers of His governance — of the created beings in general, and of all Yisrael in particular. She establishes the laws and paths of the receivers — toward which all the paths of influence are directed.27 She oversees the receiving created beings. Nukva receives the abundance from the male — from Z"A — and he, as stated, receives it from the Partzufim above him. She clothes Z"A from his midpoint downward — that is, from there she receives his influence. According to her preparation she unites with him and receives from him the abundance — in order to distribute it to the created beings. Her preparation for the union depends on the deeds of the lower beings — for through their evil deeds they blemish her, G-d forbid — until she is not fit to receive — and they cause a separation between her and Z"A. But through their good deeds they complete her — until she is fit to receive the full influence — and they bring her to cleaving with Z"A and cause her union with him: the union of the Holy One Blessed be He (the governance of influence — Z"A) with His Shechinah (— Nukva) — to receive the abundance for Yisrael who cleave to the Shechinah.

segments.en: Let us add an explanation: "union" (zivug) is a cooperation between two different forces — Sefiros or Partzufim. Through their joining — their union — a joint action emerges between them: a third power, Sefirah, Partzuf, or abundance. What is the nature of the union — the partnership — between Z"A and Nukva, between the giver and the receiver? For the giver is active while the receiver is only passive — so how is a cooperation between them possible — which is the matter of the union? We learn here a great principle in the service of the created beings — the receivers. His will, blessed be He, is to influence and to benefit the creatures; but the realisation of this will depends on the preparation of the receivers — on their merit and their refinement through their good deeds: to be fit to receive. The more the created beings complete themselves — the more the Holy One Blessed be He can influence; through this they fulfil more of His will — which is to benefit and to influence. Through this the created beings are truly partners in the bringing down of the abundance — this is the matter of their union with the Influencer. In the words of Rabbenu: "This is their merit — that they fulfilled the desire of the Emanator, blessed be He, Who desires that His existents receive His goodness."28

segments.en: In summary: A"K clothes itself through its Sefirah of Malchus into the World of Atzilus — for the Malchus of A"K becomes the Partzuf of Atik, and the seven lower Sefiros of Atik clothe themselves in the entire height of the Partzuf of A"A. A"A extends the entire length of the World of Atzilus — from its head to its end. The two Partzufim of Abba and Imma — which transfer the abundance of perfection from A"A to Z"A — clothe A"A from below his head to his midpoint — but the head of A"A is not clothed. Z"A clothes A"A from his midpoint downward — and Z"A himself is clothed from his midpoint downward by Nukva.

ח.
segments.en: The three principal Partzufim of the World of Atzilus are: A"A, Z"A, Nuk'. (Av"A are only the connectors between A"A and Zu"N — and they beget and complete them.) Arich Anpin — great of face, whose attribute is complete and perfect Chesed — brings the world through all the events of time to perfection and to the annulment of evil in the future. Zair Anpin is the governance of judgment that prevails in actuality as long as there is evil in Creation. Nukva is the root of the receivers of governance — the created beings — who according to their deeds she rises and falls — fitting to receive for them abundantly or sparingly. We are thus taught that the three principal Partzufim encompass the three fundamentals of Creation: the Purpose — perfection (A"A); the Action — the laws of Divine service (Z"A); the Actors — the creatures (Nuk' — who is their root). These three Partzufim — A"A, Z"A, and Nuk' — stand vertically: along the height of the World of Atzilus, one below the other. Z"A clothes A"A from his midpoint downward — and Nuk' clothes Z"A from his midpoint downward. The rule is: the higher the Partzuf (or the higher the world) — the more abundant is his Chesed. A"A in his essence is complete Chesed. On the other hand, Nukva is in the aspect of Din — for the receiver is limited and constricted in her capacity for receiving, according to what is due her through Din. Z"A — who influences Nuk' — relative to her is in the aspect of Chesed. But his measure of Chesed is small ("zeir") compared to the great Chesed of A"A ("arich"). Thus he is intermediate between A"A and Nuk' — in the aspect of Rachamim. According to this, one can also view the three Partzufim horizontally — in a row from right to left — in the aspect of Chesed-Din-Rachamim: A"A on the right, in the aspect of Chesed; Z"A in the centre, in the aspect of Rachamim; Nukva on the left, in the aspect of Din.29

י.
segments.en: As stated above: the Sefirah of Malchus of a higher world becomes Keser for the world below it. Just as Atik (which is the Malchus of A"K) clothes itself in Atzilus — so too Nukva (which is the Malchus of Atzilus) clothes herself in the World of Briyah and becomes for it the aspect of Atik — and thereby connects the World of Briyah to the World of Atzilus. Similarly the Malchus of Briyah — its Nukva — becomes Atik for Yetzirah; and in the same way Yetzirah is connected with Asiyah. In the worlds of Briyah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah the same structure of the five Partzufim with their branches exists — but in each world the Sefiros and Partzufim operate according to the nature of that world, as explained above in the section "Worlds."

segments.en: Inner Light, Surrounding Light

רא שונה .כנגדם באי׳ — קטנות וגדלות שנייה .כענינו ברא שונה ענינו ב שנייה .שמוחין הרא שונים מלמטה ,וה שניים מלמעלה.
segments.en: The light that the vessel is capable of containing — this is its inner light. The remaining light that cannot enter the vessel — hovers over it from outside. This is the surrounding light, which illuminates the vessel from a distance; therefore its effect on the vessel is limited. The inner light operates in the vessel to refine and purify it, so that it can contain additional light. This is the reciprocal relationship between light and vessel: the vessel constricts the light; on the other hand, the light purifies the vessel and weakens its power of constriction. Then additional light from the surrounding light is able to enter the vessel and continue to purify and expand it — and prepare it for the entry of even more light; and so on. Light and vessel are the roots of soul and body — and their reciprocal relationship. The body impedes the entry of the light of the soul and limits its dominance. But on the other hand — the more the soul dominates the body and subjects it to the service of Hashem — the more it purifies it, and prepares it to receive within itself additional parts of the light of the soul that previously only hovered over it from above in the aspect of surrounding light.

segments.en: The description of the structure of the worlds and Partzufim above relates to the worlds in their rectified state — but preceding them were stages of breaking and destruction, and after them came stages of rectification. Our Sages of blessed memory said [Bereishis Rabbah 3:9]: "R' Avahu said: this teaches that He was creating worlds and destroying them, until He created these ones. He said — these please Me, those do not please Me." The destruction of the worlds — the Shevirah (Breaking) — and their re-creation — the World of Tikkun — is one of the central topics in Chochmas HaEmes, for this is the root of all possibility of rectification and corruption for man.

אבא
segments.en: A brief and fundamental preliminary principle of Chochmas HaEmes: "there is nothing new under the sun" — all possible descents and ascents were already prepared from the very beginning of Creation. Our Sages of blessed memory said [Bereishis Rabbah 3:10]: "R' Yanai said: from the beginning of the creation of the world the Holy One Blessed be He foresaw the deeds of the righteous and the deeds of the wicked. 'And the earth was chaos and void' — these are the deeds of the wicked; 'And G-d said let there be light' — these are the deeds of the righteous" — see there. Chochmas HaEmes teaches: how the Holy One Blessed be He prepared at the beginning of Creation — through foreseeing — the paths of rectification for the righteous, and the paths of corruption for the wicked.32 The stages of the destruction and rectification of the worlds and their re-building prepared the possibilities of descent and ascent for man.

segments.en: We shall describe the Shevirah and the Tikkun in broad strokes — without entering into the particulars of their causes and their detailed consequences. As mentioned above — ten Sefiros emerged from the eyes of A"K. First their ten vessels emerged, and then their ten lights emerged — which entered into the vessels. The three vessels of Keser, Chochmah, and Binah were able to receive the lights — for they were rectified, pure, and refined. But the seven lower vessels were not perfect — for various reasons there were in them impurities — unrefined parts — and therefore they could not receive their lights. When the lights entered into them — the vessels broke and fell from the World of Atzilus to the worlds of Briyah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah — but their lights remained in the World of Atzilus. This stage is called the World of Tohu — the world in a corrupted state. Afterward a new light emerged — ten Sefiros from the brow of A"K — in order to rectify the broken vessels. The broken vessels ascended and returned to the World of Atzilus, were rectified there, and their lights re-entered them. In combination with the ten Sefiros that emerged from the brow of A"K — from them all the Partzufim and Worlds were built. The building of the worlds after the Shevirah — which was discussed above — is the World of Tikkun.

א.
segments.en:
The impurities that were in the vessels — which caused their imperfection and their breaking — were separated and removed from the vessels through the Shevirah. When the vessels were re-created, the impurities did not serve as material for building the vessels — only from the finest parts were the Worlds of Tikkun and their Partzufim built. (The Shevirah and Tikkun were compared to a golden vessel with impurities — in order to purify it one breaks it and melts it in the smelting furnace; through this the impurities come out, and one pours it anew — complete and pure of impurities.) From these impurities — which remained after the rectification of the vessels — the structure of the Sitra Achra was built: it too is built in the form of four worlds with their Partzufim, for "this one corresponding to that one did G-d make" [Koheles 7:14]. But the place where the Sitra Achra stands is at the bottom of Asiyah. Through his evil deeds man strengthens its power and might, G-d forbid — until it can gain control in the worlds and Partzufim of holiness that parallel its own worlds and Partzufim — and again mix back into the vessels — causing a regression toward the Shevirah, G-d forbid. On the other hand — every good deed strengthens the light, and this subdues and diminishes the dominion of the Sitra Achra — which can spread only in the concealment of the light; and a little light pushes away much darkness. The complete clarification of the vessels from the admixture of impurities has not yet been completed in the creation of the World of Tikkun. There also remain within the impurities sparks of holiness — which descended with the vessels at the time of their breaking and falling — that need to be elevated through the use of the world's necessities for Divine service — and through this to bring them into the building of the World of Tikkun. Man's task is to complete and perfect the Tikkun of the world and to beware of corrupting it. Every commandment and every abstention from transgression are further steps toward the clarification and complete Tikkun — until evil is annulled from the world and everything arrives at its complete rectification with the help of the Creator of the world.

segments.en: We have endeavoured with Heavenly help to present to the reader the form of the "Tree of Descent" in sharp conciseness33 — and all the rest: go and study: in the book Pischay Chochmah VaDaas, in the ten chapters of Klalus HaIlan, and in Klalei Chochmas HaEmes — which describe in brief principles what is stated in the writings of the Ari z"l. The source of the explanations presented — and additional explanations — will be found in Maamar HaVikuach, in the letters of Rabbenu at the end of Sefer Pischay Chochmah VaDaas, in Sefer Daas Tevunos and the Sefer HaKlalim appended to it, in Sefer Klah Pischay Chochmah, in Sefer Adir Bamarom, and in the rest of Rabbenu's books.

segments.en: It is superfluous to emphasise that all the explanations given here are only one of the faces out of the seventy faces of Chochmas HaEmes. As stated at the beginning of our words — preceding all the explanations is knowledge of the Sacred Tree in its structure and particulars. This knowledge is the cornerstone and the peg by which one enters the gates of the inner understanding of the Torah, the words of our Sages of blessed memory and their mysteries, the commandments from the Torah and from Rabbinic decree — their enactments and their ordinances; man — his body and soul in all their parts; the world and all that is in it;34 prayer and its intentions; the paths of repentance and its rectifications; the seasons of the year — weekdays and holy days; all the eras of the days of the world — their ascents and descents and all their events; and the worlds of eternal reward. All these are subjects of the eight gates of the writings of the Ari z"l and his other works — which are founded upon the Torah of Rashbi z"tzal — explained in various ways by the commentators on his Torah. Foundations and keys to understanding them are given and explained to us in a clear manner in the writings of our great master, the Ramchal z"tzal.

ה.
segments.en: We pray to the Giver of the Torah: "Uncover my eyes and I shall behold wonders from Your Torah" [Tehillim 119:18]. Just as we merited a trace of sparks from the wonders of His Torah through His boundless Chesed as an unearned gift — so may we merit to see the splendour of its brilliantly shining lights. In the words of Rashi [Shir HaShirim 1:2] — that Yisrael are "assured by Him that He will again appear upon them, to explain to them the secret of its reasons and the concealment of its hidden things; and they await His face to fulfil His word — and this is: 'Let Him kiss me with the kisses of His mouth.'" Speedily in our days with the coming of our righteous Messiah.

segments.en: Thanks and praise to the Creator of the world for our meriting to bring to light the book "Pischay Chochmah VaDaas" by our great master, the man of G-d, Rabbi Moshe Chaim Luzzatto z"tzal, in a corrected and improved edition. The work was called by its author "Klalim Shniyim" (Second Principles) — for he preceded it with the First Principles, in which the general foundations of Chochmas HaEmes are explained, which we printed in Sefer Daas Tevunos — Sefer HaKlalim from p. 293 onward. Since this work was called by its first editor, R' Shmuel Luria z"tzal, "Pischay Chochmah VaDaas" — and by that name it became known — we retained this name for the work.

ה.
segments.en: The book Pischay Chochmah VaDaas is a wonderful abridgment of the Torah of the Ari z"l — expounded at length in Eitz Chaim and his other works. It brings from the Torah of the Ari z"l all the root matters in clear order and in golden language. Therefore it also serves as a guide to us — what counts as the root topics.1 We receive a general and ordered view of the structure of the worlds and their Partzufim — from the beginning of Creation — the Tzimtzum of His light — to the end of the lowest world: the World of Asiyah. The student merits to have his learning arranged in his mouth — and his knowledge in Chochmas HaEmes will not be a multiplicity of unordered particulars — but each matter properly in its place, illuminated by the clear explanations of Rabbenu.

segments.en: But here there is not only summary, synopsis, and arrangement — but an abundance of explanations of the Torah of the Ari z"l embedded between the lines. For in the course of his words, Rabbenu takes apart and arranges and resolves contradictions between different transmissions of R' Chaim Vital z"tzal who recorded the words of the Ari z"l — which the commentators of the Torah of the Ari z"l debated, each resolving them in his own way. In several places we pointed out examples of these gems. One who studies the book carefully will find many more resolutions and wondrous innovations.

segments.en: But Rabbenu follows his holy way — that he does not raise and resolve explicitly, as he writes to the Maharyi Bassan z"tzal regarding these principles:2 "And I did not note the difficulties and their resolutions — but rather I laid down the premises, through which the difficulties will collapse by themselves." And there below in his letter he writes: "The Second Principles are very lengthy — therefore I could not send them to you. But in them many difficulties and questions about the words of the Ari z"l are resolved — all in this way: premises that cause the difficulties to fall on their own." This requires of the student to be precise in Rabbenu's words. At times Rabbenu alludes that he is resolving topics that are apparently contradictory — by emphasising and saying: "and the truth is..."

segments.en: This work parallels, as stated, "Klalus HaIlan HaKadosh." The roots of Chochmas HaEmes that he encompassed there in ten chapters in sharp conciseness — Rabbenu explains them more at length in our work. It is thus found that this work is also a commentary on Klalus HaIlan. Therefore we noted the parallel section of Klalus HaIlan after the heading of each chapter — so that the student can study and see the summary of each chapter in the parallel section in Klalus HaIlan — and sometimes the one teaches about the other with additional clarification. But in the arrangement of chapters there is a difference — for in our work Rabbenu placed first the structure and clothing of the Partzufim and the rectifications of the Partzufim — and brought them at the head of the work in the First and Second Principles. But in Klalus HaIlan they appear according to the order of the chain-descent of the worlds and Partzufim — in the seventh and eighth chapters.

segments.en: We advise the beginning student entering Chochmas HaEmes to study according to the order of Klalus HaIlan HaKadosh — that is, to skip at the beginning over Principle One and Principle Two, and to begin from Principle Three (ch. 26) — which speaks of the beginning of Creation — and to study through the end of Principle Three (ch. 78), and then return to Principles One and Two — and then continue with Principle Four (ch. 79). Principle Four has no parallel in Klalus HaIlan HaKadosh (other than the last chapters from ch. 92 onward) — for it does not deal with the structure of the Tree of Descent, but explains general principles on inner dimension and outer dimension, the drawing of abundance, etc. These matters are foundational and illuminating — for understanding the depth of the order of the chain-descent. But a student who wishes at the beginning of his study to engage with knowing the chain-descent and structure of the worlds and Partzufim — can skip most of this Principle. Principle Five and Principle Six deal with the branches of the World of Atzilus — the worlds of Briyah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah, angels and souls, and the powers of the Sitra Achra. Here Rabbenu expands the discussion of particulars not included in Klalus HaIlan HaKadosh. Here too one can skip at the beginning of study — and take Klalus HaIlan HaKadosh as sufficient — to know what belongs to the primary knowledge of the chain-descent and structure of the worlds. After the chain-descent and structure of the worlds is clear before the student's eyes — he can complete his study in the remaining chapters of the book.

segments.en: Rabbenu uses concise and golden language — and encompasses much in few words. Therefore we added explanations and notes compiled by Torah scholars in collaborative learning with Heavenly help. The need to explain the work was already seen by the student R' Yekusiel Gordon of Vilna. segments.en: Sefer Pischay Chochmah VaDaas was first published in Warsaw in the year 5625 by R' Sh. Luria — from a manuscript that was in the manuscript treasury of the Gaon of Vilna z"tzal — as noted on the title page of the book.4 Since then it was printed in several photographic editions together with Sefer Klah Pischay Chochmah. Due to the multiplicity of errors and omissions in that edition — the work was not usable and was considered a sealed book. In the present edition the book was corrected with Heavenly help from several manuscripts that came from the study house of the Ramchal — among them the Columbia University manuscript, New York, no. 89k17, and the Mantua manuscript no. 97. Our thanks are extended to these libraries.

ו.
segments.en: Notes of R' Yekusiel: a. Speaking of the World of Atzilus — from which all the worlds were drawn. b. And if you ask: does not the Zohar speak only of five Partzufim — A"A, Av"A, and Zu"N? One can answer: because he goes on to explain the matter of the Mochin that come from Av"A through the primary and secondary Yesodos in their gadlus and katnus — and through this they become Partzufim in their own right. Also the matter of the unions performed through the prayers — which differ in each one: sometimes Yisrael and Leah, sometimes Ya'akov and Rachel, sometimes Yisrael and Rachel. Therefore he counted here twelve Partzufim. But the principal Partzufim are five. c. A Partzuf is called one Sefirah that is revealed to operate by itself in one particular form. That is: the Sefiros number ten — KhB, ChG"T, NHY"M — and they are the ten Sefiros of A"A from the beginning of Atzilus to its end. Afterward they divide into Partzufim — then Keser is considered the Partzuf of A"A, and Chochmah is considered the Partzuf of Abba, and Binah the Partzuf of Imma, and ChG"T NHY — which are the six extremities — are considered the Partzuf of Z"A, and the Sefirah of Malchus is considered the Partzuf of Nuk'. If we consider for example the Sefirah of Chochmah as one of the Sefiros according to the World of Atzilus — then it is called by the name Sefirah — for it is one Sefirah of the ten. But when we consider the Sefirah of Chochmah for the particular operations found in it according to the lights shining in their particularity — then it is called according to this: the Partzuf. And it counts as the Partzuf of Abba with the number 613 — shining in its ten Sefiros. But if it is considered only as a Sefirah — then among all of them we discern the number 613. d. One clothing the other. The lower clothes the upper — and the upper is clothed by it from within.

segments.en: And now I shall explain the order of clothing: A"A and his Female are the innermost of allj — for the right side of A"A is his male aspect, and the left side of him is his female. On his two arms Av"A clothe themselves: Abba on the right and Imma on the left. Their ChB"D are the first sections12 of the arms; their ChG"T are the middle sections; their NHY are the lower sections. And the throat of A"A — which is his Binah — is their Keser.4 And they reach as far as the navel of A"A.14 Also his body — which is his Tiferes — as far as this navel remains covered: half by Abba15 and half by Imma.

segments.en: From the chest of Av"A downward, the primary Yesodos6 clothe themselves: their Keser at the chest; their ChB"D in the first sections of the NHY of Av"A;7 their ChG"T in the second sections; their NHY in the third sections. And from their chest downward, the secondary Yesodos clothe in the order just described. All of them are found to reach as far as the navel of A"A;8 but afterward8* their legs extend to clothe Z"A — and with him they then reach to the end of the world. Now since Av"A clothe themselves within the primary Yesodos — and the primary Yesodos within the secondary Yesodos — in the place where they clothe themselves they are no longer called by their own name; rather from there upward the entirety of their Partzuf is counted. And in the place from which they clothe downward — they make for themselves new NHY. It is thus found that Av"A properly speaking are called only until the chest of A"A — for from there downward they are called Yesodos.

segments.en: From the chest of the Yesodos9 downward, Z"A10 clothes himself to the end of Atzilus — and then new NHY are made for the Yesodos12 as well. And the primary NHY clothe themselves within Z"A in this order: the NHY of Yisrael Saba clothe themselves within the NHY of Tevunah — and the NHY of Tevunah within Z"A13 — in the order described: Tiferes in Keser; the upper sections of NHY in ChB"D; the second sections in ChG"T; the third sections in NHY. But one must know that Yesod has only two sections. And there is also a difference between the male Yesod and the female Yesod: the female Yesod is shorter — being only one and a half sections — while the male Yesod is two sections. Accordingly, the Yesod of Tevunah ends at the chest of Z"A. But the Yesod of Yisrael Saba extends further downward from there.14 And the new NHY descend along the back of Z"A — reaching as far as approximately his Tiferes.15

segments.en: And sometimes Rachel stands back-to-back with Z"A from his chest downward — and then Ya'akov stands behind him facing the back of Z"A. And sometimes she comes face-to-face with Z"A — and then Z"A stands in the middle with Ya'akov and Rachel on either side of him, facing each other — and all three see one another. And Leah also sometimes stands at the back of Z"A — her face at his back. And when Rachel is also there at the back — her feet stand within the head of Rachel.20 And sometimes she comes face-to-face with Yisrael who is Z"A — from his chest upward — and new NHY are made for him21 — as we said regarding Av"A.22 These are the twelve Partzufim — through whose combination23 the Chariot is made.

segments.en: And Leah also has many aspects — for she emerges from the Malchusos: namely from the Crowns26 of Av"A that are within Z"A. And behold: the Crown of the Yesod of Abba in its place produces one Leah — and the Crown of the Yesod of Imma produces another Leah. Then the radiance of the Crown of the Yesod of Abba pierces the Yesod of Imma and produces another Leah outward. And all of these are still within Z"A. Then the radiance of the Crown of the Yesod of Imma pierces further — and also pierces the body of Z"A — and brings out another radiance; and this is the principal Leah of which we speak.27 All of this is the totality of the Chariot.

segments.en: And above all of them there is Atik — upon which the Chariot28 is suspended and encompassed. And this Atik is the Malchus of Adam Kadmon the Hidden One — who is sometimes called by the name Ein Sof as well. And this Atik has ten Sefiros: the side of his face is called his male aspect, and the side of his back is called his female aspect. And the three upper Sefiros of this female29 are above all of Atzilus — and are called Reisha d'Lo Isyada (the Head That Is Not Known). And her seven lower Sefiros clothe themselves within A"A. And this is their order: Chesed in Keser;30 Gevurah in Chochmah; Tiferes in Binah; the first sections of NHY in Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferes; the second sections in NHY; the third sections of Netzach, Hod31 together with Malchus — in the Malchus of A"A.

מדאה מקומות
segments.en: In this Klal we shall explain the particulars of the Tikkunim — the rectifications33 — found in the Partzufim; from all of them is built the form34 of the supernal Chariot. And all of theseb are rectifications that stand for the sake of governance — to prepare the influence so that it be neither too little nor too much beyond what is needed for the receivers.

רמח״ל ענק עשר ספירות (וכל הספרים מלאים מזה) ,ובקל׳׳ח פ״ח סימן ו׳ ,כל ספירה היא מדה אחת מן המדות של א״ס ב׳׳ה אשר ברא את העולמות ומנהג אותם כר ע״ש, ובנפש החיים ש״ב פ״ב .עשר עיגולים ויושדם כר ,עגץ עיגולים ויושר ,בפתחי חכמה סימן י״ג בביאור באריכות ,ובדברי הגר״א ז״ל שם כתב ג״כ מ ה יעו״ש בזה׳׳ל דש ב׳ מיני השגחות בכלל ובפרט וכר ,תהו עיגולים דושר יעו״ש מ׳׳ש בזה .מנהיג כר, כידוע שהכל נכלל בשלשה חסד או דין או הנהגה ממוצעת שנקרא רחמים שסימנם הד׳׳ר ,והם לשכר ולעונש וכר ,ע׳ פתחי חכמה סימן ד וש״מ ,ובפי ,הגר״א על ס׳׳ד דף א׳ ע״ד ביאור זה .ומחדר כל רעה לטובה ,זה מבואר באורך בם׳ פתחי חכמה בכמה מקומות איך שעיקר כל הדברים להחדר הרע לטוב ,דעדין בפרט בסימן ב׳ ד׳ כ״ז ל׳ מ׳׳א מ״ז מ״ח מ׳׳ט וכל הספר מלא מזה ,וכן מ״ש ומחדר כל בריותיו לרצונו ,מבואר שם ובסי׳ ב׳ הנ׳׳ל .וכן הוא אומר אני ראשון ואני אחרון ,ע׳ שם פ׳׳ח סימן ט״ז .ואומר כל הנקרא בשמי ולכבודי בראתיו וכו׳ ,ע׳׳ש בסי׳ ל״ט בזה׳׳ל :כי כל נברא לכבוד הבורא והוא ענק כל פועל ד׳ למענהו וכר . (מ״ב) פנימיות ,חיצוניות ,פנימיות מבחינת הקו ,וחיצוניות מבחינת הרשימו שנשאר במקום המצומצם ,והוא נתבאר במקומות שנתבאר הצמצום וקו כנ׳׳ל ,ובפרט בפתחי חכמה סימן כ״ז כ״ח כ״ט ,ובסימן ל״ה ,ובסימן מ׳׳א ,וש״מ .כמראה אדם ,ענק אדם הנזכר ,וכל פרטי דמות אדם נתבאר בספרו קנאת ד׳ צבאות ,הנדפס ג״כ בסוף ס׳ מגן וצינה בשם הרמ׳׳ח לוצאטו זללה״ה שם בביאור על כל עניני איברים שבאדם המחכר, וכן מבואר מזה בפתחי חכמה סימן י״ב ובסימן י״ז ,וסימן ע׳ ע׳׳א ,ושאר מקומות בספרו הנ״ל .ובנפש החיים שער א׳ פ״ו ,וש״ב פ׳׳ה( ,ולא נצטרך לרשום עוד במקום שמחכרים שמות איברים שבאדם) .אדם קדמון ,בכללות ענינו הוא מדובר באורך בפתחי חכמה מן סי׳ ל״א עד סימן ל״ו באורך ענינו וכל עניני אורות שלו ,וכל המדובר בו הכל מבואר שם ,וש״מ בספרו ,ובכלל כל הענינים הנראה ומחכר ,מבואר בפתחי חכמה סימן ז׳ ח׳ ט׳ ענק מראות המוזכר בהם וכנ׳׳ל .ארבעה חושים ,מבואר שם בסימן ל׳׳ב ל״ד. (מ״ג) ד׳ אותיות הד״׳ה בכל י ׳ מלואים כו׳ ,ע״ש בסימן ל״א באורך ,בסימן כ׳׳ב, ביאור זה ובסימן נ״ה נ׳׳ו .טעמים נקודות תגץ אותיות ,שם בפתחי חכמה סימן י״ט כ׳ כ״א כ-ב כ״ג ,וענק טנת״א ע״ע שם סוף סימן ל׳׳א ,ובנפש החיים שער שני פ׳ ט״ז ובהג״ה שם .ע׳י׳ב בגולגלת וענפיו נעלמות כר ,מבואר בפתחי חכמה סימן ל״ג .מן השערות של הראש כו׳ ,שם סימן ל״ג( ,וע״ש סי׳ ק׳׳ה) ,ובדברי הרמ״ח לוצאטו שבס״ס מגן וצינה ובהערה שם ,ובביאור הגר״א ז״ל על שה״ש(ה׳ ט״ו) .ותנא ס׳׳ג כר ,שם סי׳ ל״ג ,וכל הענק מבואר שם יעו״ש .תחתונים גפה כו׳ ,ענק אורות אתן חוטם פה ועולם העקודים ,מבואר בפתחי חכמה שהם ההנהגות שיהיה אחר הששת אלפים שנה ,וכתב שם בסימן צ״ז בענק האורות דאח״פ הנ״ל שהוא מאלף השביעי ודלאה כד .אך בזד .הזמן צריך לחלק בק זמן העליות והוא עד אלף העשירי שמגיעים כר יעו״ש ,וביותר ביאור בפ״ח ודעת ד׳ כ״ד ,וכן בסי׳ מ״ט האריך שאחר ששת אלפים יהיה בסוד עולם עקודים יעו׳׳ש ח״ב הבחנה י״ג .אלו מנימיס ואלו מקיפים לגביהם כר ,ענק אור פנימי ואור מקיף בפתחי חכמה סימן כ״ח כ״ט .ואלו נכללים בה׳ אחת כו׳ ,ענק האותיות המחכר בכ״מ ,ע׳ פתחי חכמה סימן י״ט כ׳ כ״א כ״ל כ״ג יעו״ש ,וביותר ביאור ענק האותיות שנדרש כאן מבואר בסימן ל״ה .והרי נתקרבו זח לזה ,ביאור זה בסימן ל״ג ,ע״ש כל הענק מדוע מתחלה אור פנימי ומקיף רחוקים זה מזה ,ואח״כ הולכים ומתקרבים יעו״ש. (מ׳׳ד) וכח הכלי בלוע בהם ,מבואר בסימן ל״ה .ודאשון שבהם חזר ונכנס כר ,ע״ש
